title: Renaissance Babylonian Hours Clock
intro: This clock represents the Renaissance European convention of counting equal hours from sunrise. It is distinct from the ancient Mesopotamian beru and ush model.
structure: The display starts at 00:00 BAB-R at computed sunrise. Hours are ordinary elapsed hours, with 60 minutes per hour and optional seconds; the next sunrise resets the reading. Because consecutive sunrises are not exactly 24 hours apart, the count can briefly reach or exceed 24.
example: If the calculated sunrise were 06:20, the reading at 09:35 would be 03:15 BAB-R. At the next calculated sunrise the reading returns to 00:00, not at conventional midnight.
history: Renaissance gnomonic traditions included sunrise-origin hour counting, alongside sunset-origin Italian hours. These names refer to distinct historical display conventions.
model: The provider computes sunrise using compact solar equation-of-time and declination terms, latitude, east-positive longitude and a 0.833-degree horizon correction. It selects the latest valid event in a bounded search, floors elapsed ordinary seconds, and formats hours, minutes and optional seconds. It searches for the first visible change at millisecond resolution.
limits: The solar origin is calculated, not directly observed. Invalid coordinates fail and a missing origin produces N/A rather than a fabricated sunrise. Time zones and daylight saving do not change the solar calculation. No universal Renaissance locality or historical instrument is reconstructed. The solar model assumes an idealised sea-level horizon and standard depression; local terrain and weather are not modelled.
